title: A little girl handed me a note on a flight to Chicago. It said, "Please pretend you're my grandma. The man next to me isn't my dad." (PART 2)

blocks.text: …missing. Her father has full custody. There's a court order. I'm just the one she paid to fly her."
I didn't let go of Lily's hand. "Then you can explain that to the police," I said.

He sat back and stared at his phone for the rest of the descent. We landed in Omaha. Two police officers and an FBI agent boarded before anyone was allowed to stand. They asked the man to come with them. He didn't resist.
A flight attendant let me stay with Lily while the agent talked to her in a quiet office at the airport. Over the next few hours, I learned the rest.

Lily's parents had divorced the year before. A judge gave her father custody after her mother, Dana, stopped taking her medication for bipolar disorder and twice disappeared with Lily for days. Dana was allowed supervised visits.

That morning, during a visit at a Denver park, she'd slipped away from the social worker and handed Lily to a former coworker she'd paid two thousand dollars to fly her daughter to a relative in Chicago. The social worker reported Lily missing within minutes. An alert went out an hour after we took off.

Lily knew something was wrong because her mother had always told her never to get on a plane with someone she didn't know. The man was a stranger to her. So she found the grandmotherly woman in the next seat.

Her father, Mark, drove through the night from Denver. When he walked into the airport office the next morning, Lily ran into his arms so hard she knocked him back a step. He thanked me through tears.
The man was charged with aiding custodial interference. Dana was found at a Chicago bus station later that day.
She was charged too, but the judge ordered treatment instead of jail. Mark told me she's back on her medication and has supervised visits again. Lily draws her a picture for every one.
I missed Thanksgiving with my sister that year. But every November now, I get a card from Denver with a crayon drawing of an airplane and two people holding hands in row fourteen.
If you have information about a missing child, contact the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children at 1-800-843-5678. For mental health support, call or text 988.
